title: Mitigate execution-path oscillation from speculative kernel probing and attention autotiling
creator: Aisha Nair
description:
Summary: During a narrow window following the scheduler refactor deployed 2025-02-08 we observed sustained p95/p99 token latency increases and transient throughput collapse across several customer workloads. Root cause analysis indicates a feedback loop between the new speculative kernel-probing behavior and the attention autotiling heuristic: speculative probes caused rapid kernel affinity flips when sequence-length distributions or KV cache warmup patterns changed, which in turn caused attention autotiler to recompute tiling choices frequently. The recompute + kernel switch path is expensive and occasionally triggered KV-cache thrash, amplifying latency and per-token cost.

Impact: Multiple hosted customers and Dedicated pools saw 2x-4x p99 token latency spikes for ~18 minutes during the incident window. Some long-running streaming sessions experienced stalls requiring client reconnects. No data corruption or security impact identified.

Reproduction notes: Synthetic repro harness created by load-generator v2 reproduces oscillation when traffic mixes short (<=64) and long (>=1024) sequences with a 30:1 short:long ratio and with cold KV cache. Steps: 1) start runtime with scheduler-refactor flags; 2) run mixed-seq workload; 3) observe kernel probe logs and autotile recalculations; 4) capture per-request kernel_id transitions and KV cache miss rates. Repro artifacts: synthetic-bench-oscillation.ipynb and experiment config available in Drive: https://drive.internal/redwood/experiments/oscillation-2025-02-09

Immediate mitigation applied: rolled back speculative probing to conservative mode (scheduler flag probe_mode=conservative) and applied a 300ms debounce on autotiler recompute while we build a permanent fix. This reduced p99 back to baseline.

Long-term action plan (owners & ETA):
- Implement kernel-selection hysteresis with configurable stability window and transition cost accounting (owner: Jin Park, ETA: 2025-02-28).
- Add autotiler change-rate limiter and rate-aware cost model that considers ongoing kernel changes (owner: Marco Delgado, ETA: 2025-03-07).
- Expand telemetry: per-request kernel_history, autotile_decision_id, kv_cache_eviction_events to be exported to traces and a new dashboard (owner: Sara Liu, ETA: 2025-02-21).
- Canary + automated rollback policy: ship canary flag to 5% of traffic with automatic rollback if p95 increases >15% (owner: Tomás Rivera, ETA: 2025-03-03).
- Update scheduler probe to be bounded and context-aware (avoid probing when KV-cache recently evicted or when sequence-length distribution is unstable) (owner: Jin Park, ETA: 2025-03-10).
- Post-deploy synthetic validation: add the mixed-seq test into continuous regression suite and gate runtime releases on no-oscillation signal for 2 consecutive runs (owner: QA team, ETA: 2025-02-24).

Acceptance criteria: hysteresis + autotile limiter in place; canary pipeline active; dashboards show kernel flip rate and autotile recompute rate with alert when flip rate > 0.05 flips/sec per GPU; regression tests added to CI and green for 48h.

Rollout strategy: implement fix behind a feature-flag toggled off by default. Deploy to canary pool (5%), monitor the new telemetry for 48 hours, then ramp to 25% and 100% with staged gates. If any gate fires, auto-revert to conservative probing mode.

Documentation & training: update Runtime Operations runbook with detection playbook, quick rollback command, and context on tuning hysteresis and autotile parameters. Add a short postmortem writeup for the Incident Channel and customer-facing summary for affected customers (owner: Aisha Nair, ETA: 2025-02-20).
